## 4. Read a chord from a transposed score

Four instruments each hold one note. Work out what each one sounds, then name the chord. Open the answer
when you have it.

<div class="abc-ex" data-sound="piano"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
L:1/1
%%score 1 2 3 4
V:1 name="Clarinet in B♭" clef=treble
V:2 name="Alto sax" clef=treble
V:3 name="Horn in F" clef=treble
V:4 name="Viola" clef=alto
K:C
[V:1] d |]
[V:2] e |]
[V:3] B |]
[V:4] C |]
</script></div>

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Answer

Clarinet written D5 sounds C5 (a 2nd lower). Alto sax written E5 sounds G4 (a 6th lower). Horn written B4
sounds E4 (a 5th lower). Viola reads at pitch: middle C. The chord is **C major**: C4, E4, G4, C5.
:::

## 5. Unison or not?

A flute, a B♭ clarinet and a horn in F play this bar from a transposed score. Do they play the same notes?

<div class="abc-ex" data-sound="piano"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/4
%%score 1 2 3
V:1 name="Flute" clef=treble
V:2 name="Clarinet in B♭" clef=treble
V:3 name="Horn in F" clef=treble
K:G
[V:1] G A B c |]
[V:2] [K:A] A B c d |]
[V:3] [K:D] d e f g |]
</script></div>

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Answer

Yes. Concert key G major: the clarinet part is in A major (a 2nd up) and the horn in D major (a 5th up).
All three sound G4, A4, B4, C5: a unison.
:::

## 6. Read the alto and tenor lines

Sing or play each line before pressing ▶, then check yourself.

<div class="abc-ex" data-sound="piano"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
T:Viola (alto clef)
M:3/4
L:1/4
K:F clef=alto
F A c | B G E | F2 C | F3 |]
</script></div>

<div class="abc-ex" data-sound="piano"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
T:Cello (tenor clef)
M:4/4
L:1/4
K:G clef=tenor
G, B, D G | F D E C | B, D A, C | G,4 |]
</script></div>

## 7. Make your own

## Works Cited

<!-- works-cited: written by scripts/works-cited.py -->
::: {.works-cited}
**For students**

"Transposing Instrument." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transposing_instrument](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transposing_instrument). Concert-pitch scores (Prokofiev), horn bass clef ambiguity, crooks, brass-band trombone in B♭.

**For teachers**

Adler, Samuel. *The Study of Orchestration*. 4th ed., W. W. Norton, 2016. Instrument ranges, clefs and transpositions.

Gould, Elaine. *Behind Bars: The Definitive Guide to Music Notation*. Faber Music, 2011. Grace notes, trills and other ornaments in modern notation.
:::
